get.description: List all buckets (FS ∪ membership), including orphans and ghosts.

post.description: Create a bucket on behalf of a specified owner (admin only).

get.description: List all accounts (never includes hashes or secrets).

post.description: Create a new account. Returns the token once.

delete.description: Delete an account. Use ?cascade=true to delete owned buckets.

Create a new bucket. The creator becomes the owner.

Returns 409 if the bucket name is already taken (directory exists).
Returns 403 if the caller already owns ``max_buckets_per_account`` buckets
(per-account bucket quota).

delete.description:
Delete a bucket and all its contents (admin only).

Cleans up: filesystem directory, DB rows (membership, versions,
tombstones, bucket mapping).  Non-admin callers get 403; non-existent
or inaccessible buckets return 404.

get.description: Get bucket information including timestamps in ISO 8601 UTC with Z suffix.

List directory metadata (path + permissions) in a bucket.

Directories carry no content hash and never appear in the ``/files``
listing, so this dedicated endpoint exposes their permissions for the
download-only permission converge ("remote wins"): a peer applies a
divergent directory mode locally without any per-file event having
arrived.

Args:
    bucket: Name of the bucket to list.

Returns:
    Streamed JSON array (chunked) of ``{"path": <bucket-relative>,
    "permissions": <octal>}`` entries, in deterministic path order.

Raises:
    InvalidBucketNameError: If bucket name is invalid.
    BucketNotFoundError: If bucket does not exist.

delete.description:
Delete a file from a bucket.

Removes the file and broadcasts a "deleted" event to all
connected WebSocket clients.

Args:
    bucket: Name of the bucket containing the file.
    cid: Client ID for event broadcasting.
    filename: Path to the file within the bucket.

Returns:
    JSON response confirming deletion.

Raises:
    InvalidBucketNameError: If bucket name is invalid.
    BucketNotFoundError: If bucket does not exist.
    InvalidPathError: If path is invalid.
    HSyncFileNotFoundError: If file does not exist.
    DeleteError: If deletion fails.

get.description:
List all files in a bucket or subdirectory.

Recursively walks the directory tree and streams metadata for all
non-hidden files as a JSON array, in deterministic path order. The array is
produced incrementally (chunked), so the server holds O(directory fanout +
one entry) rather than one dict per file; consumers collect the whole array
and apply the ``mtime`` priority locally.

Args:
    bucket: Name of the bucket to list files from.
    path: Optional subdirectory path within the bucket.

Returns:
    Streamed JSON array of file metadata dictionaries.

Raises:
    InvalidBucketNameError: If bucket name is invalid.
    InvalidPathError: If path is invalid.
    BucketNotFoundError: If bucket does not exist.

patch.description:
Move a file or directory inside a bucket without transferring its bytes.

The caller (a peer running its reconcile loop) has already established that
the destination holds the same content as the stale source path; this
endpoint performs the move atomically and records the causal consequences,
so offline peers observe a rename instead of a delete plus an upload.

Args:
    bucket: Target bucket name.
    src: Bucket-relative path of the existing entry.
    dst: Bucket-relative path the entry must move to. It must not exist:
        a concurrent creator is reported as a conflict, never overwritten.
    cid: Optional originator client ID (echo suppression for the
        ``renamed`` broadcast).
    expected_sha256: Optional guard. When given for a regular file, the
        move is refused unless the current content still hashes to this
        value — a stale listing must fall back to a normal upload instead
        of moving bytes the peer did not verify.
    mtime: Optional modification time (Unix epoch seconds) applied to the
        destination, so a rename converges the local metadata an upload
        would have carried.
    permissions: Optional octal permissions applied to the destination,
        with the same rationale.

Returns:
    The destination entry (``file``, listing shape: ``filepath`` for a file,
    ``path``/``permissions`` for a directory) plus the causal ``version`` the
    caller must record as the new merge base.

Raises:
    InvalidBucketNameError: If bucket name is invalid.
    InvalidPathError: If either path is unsafe, or a symlink rename is
        attempted (links replicate through the symlink surface).
    HSyncFileNotFoundError: If the source does not exist.
    ConflictError: If the destination exists or the checksum guard fails.
    FileOperationError: If the filesystem move fails.

post.description:
Upload a file to a bucket with resumable upload support.

Handles file upload with integrity verification (SHA-256), timestamp
preservation, and permission setting. Broadcasts an "added" event
to all connected WebSocket clients.

Supports resumable uploads: if offset > 0, the incoming data is
appended to an existing partial file (.part extension).

Args:
    bucket: Target bucket name.
    cid: Client ID for event broadcasting.
    file: The file to upload.
    path: Subdirectory path within the bucket.
    ctime: Creation time as Unix epoch seconds (int) or ISO 8601 string
        (e.g. ``2025-01-15T08:30:00Z``). Naive strings are treated as UTC.
    mtime: Modification time as Unix epoch seconds (int) or ISO 8601 string
        (e.g. ``2025-01-15T08:30:00Z``). Naive strings are treated as UTC.
    sha256sum: Expected SHA-256 checksum for integrity verification.
    permissions: File permissions as an octal string (e.g., '644').
    offset: Byte offset for resumable uploads (0 for new uploads).
    size: Total file size (required for resumable uploads).

Returns:
    JSON response confirming upload or conflict if identical file exists.

Raises:
    InvalidBucketNameError: If bucket name is invalid.
    InvalidPathError: If path is invalid.
    InvalidPermissionFormatError: If permission format is invalid.
    InvalidFilenameError: If filename contains forbidden characters or is reserved.
    ChecksumMismatchError: If SHA-256 checksum verification fails.
        UploadError: If upload operation fails.
Apply a client-computed delta to the server-side base file.

get.description: Stream the parked literal payload for a valid download token.

Return block signatures of the server-side base file (upload delta).

The client compares ``sha256`` with its expected ``base_hash`` first
(early-out) and then scans its newer file against these signatures.

post.description:
Match client base signatures against the server file (download delta).

Returns ``{delta: true, ...}`` with instructions and a token URL for the
literal payload, or ``{delta: false, reason}`` when a full transfer is
cheaper (the client then falls back to a plain download).

get.description:
Download a file from a bucket with optional zstd compression.

Streams the file content as a response with appropriate headers.
If compression is enabled and beneficial, compresses the file before sending.

Args:
    request: The incoming FastAPI request.
    bucket: Name of the bucket containing the file.
    filename: Path to the file within the bucket.

Returns:
    FileResponse or Response with the file content for download.

Raises:
    InvalidBucketNameError: If bucket name is invalid.
    InvalidPathError: If path is invalid.
    HSyncFileNotFoundError: If file does not exist.

patch.description:
Apply a content-unchanged metadata change to an existing file (no payload).

Optimized branch of the upload same-SHA path: the client declares the
filename (bucket-relative), the expected permissions, an optional corrected
``mtime``, the content hash it believes the path still holds and its CID;
the server sanitizes/applies what diverges and re-broadcasts a ``modified``
event to the other connected clients. No file bytes cross the wire. Both a
chmod and a plain ``touch`` (same content, newer mtime) converge through
this route.

Args:
    bucket: Target bucket name.
    filename: Bucket-relative path of the existing file.
    permissions: Octal permission string (e.g., '644'). Special bits
        (setuid/setgid/sticky) are stripped (remote-supplied).
    cid: Client ID for event attribution (validated, optional).
    mtime: Corrected Unix mtime to propagate (0 = leave unchanged).
    vclock: JSON-encoded effective vector clock of the sender ("" = none).
    version_id: Effective version id of the sender ("" = none).
    expected_sha256: Optional guard. The caller only reached this branch
        because its content matched the listing; when the path no longer
        holds that content a concurrent write happened, so the metadata is
        NOT applied and the caller falls back to the ordinary upload path.

Returns:
    JSON response: 200 on metadata updated, 404 when the file does
    not exist.

Raises:
    InvalidBucketNameError: If bucket name is invalid.
    InvalidPathError: If path escapes the bucket.
    InvalidPermissionFormatError: If permission format is invalid.
    InvalidFilenameError: If the basename is forbidden or reserved.
    ValidationError: If the declared CID or checksum is malformed.
    ConflictError: If the path's content no longer matches the declaration.

get.description:
Get upload status for resumable uploads.

Checks if a partial file exists from a previous interrupted upload
and returns the current offset from which the client can resume.

Args:
    request: The incoming FastAPI request.
    bucket: Target bucket name.
    filename: Path to the file within the bucket.
    sha256sum: Expected SHA-256 checksum of the complete file.
    size: Expected size of the complete file.

Returns:
    JSON response with upload status:
    - offset: Number of bytes already uploaded (0 if no partial file)
    - status: "resumable" if partial file exists, "new" otherwise

Raises:
    InvalidBucketNameError: If bucket name is invalid.
    InvalidPathError: If path is invalid.
List members of a bucket (owner/admin only; member gets 403).

post.description:
Grant membership to an account (owner/admin only).

The response is uniform whether or not the target account exists;
a missing account does not create a membership but returns
the same 201 body, so the endpoint is not an account-existence oracle. The
owner can confirm the result via the member listing.

delete.description: Revoke membership (owner/admin only; last owner must transfer first).

post.description:
Transfer ownership or reclaim an orphan bucket (owner/admin only).

If the bucket has an owner, this transfers ownership (ex-owner stays
member).  If the bucket has no owner (orphan), only admin can reclaim.

get.description:
Get presence counters for the bucket share.

Returns:
    JSON response with:
    - connected: accounts currently connected to this bucket (self included)
    - total: accounts with access to this bucket (self included)

Raises:
    InvalidBucketNameError: If bucket name is invalid.
    BucketNotFoundError: If bucket is unknown or the caller has no access.

post.description:
Create a symlink inside a bucket.

The peer sends the symlink structurally (path + target); the server
creates the link in the filesystem, never dereferencing it. Escaping
targets are rejected via ``is_safe_symlink_target``.

Args:
    bucket: Target bucket name.
    path: Bucket-relative path for the symlink to create.
    target: The symlink target (what it points to).
    cid: Optional client ID (for echo suppression on LAN master;
        unused on the central server).

Returns:
    201 on success, 400 on invalid/unsafe input or non-empty directory
    at the destination.

Raises:
    InvalidBucketNameError: If bucket name is invalid.
    InvalidPathError: If path is invalid.

get.description:
List deletion markers (tombstones) for a bucket.

Returns a mapping of hashed bucket-relative path to the causal marker
(``{"sha256", "version_id", "origin_cid", "ts", "vclock"}``). Clients use
these markers to avoid resurrecting files that were deleted while they
were offline.

Args:
    request: The incoming FastAPI request.
    bucket: Name of the bucket to list tombstones from.

Returns:
    JSON response with the tombstone payload.

Raises:
    InvalidBucketNameError: If bucket name is invalid.
    BucketNotFoundError: If bucket does not exist.

post.description:
Merge deletion markers (tombstones) pushed by a client.

A client that deleted files while offline pushes its accumulated markers
at the start of each sync cycle so the server converges to the union of
all known deletions and other peers do not resurrect those files. The
merge is **causal** per marker (vector-clock dominance, deterministic
content tie-break on concurrency — never the deletion timestamp, ADR-0003);
entries are strictly validated and the store size is capped (see
``TombstoneStore.merge``).

Args:
    request: The incoming FastAPI request; the body is the JSON tombstone
        payload (mapping of hashed path to the causal
        ``{"sha256", "version_id", "origin_cid", "ts", "vclock"}`` entry).
    bucket: Name of the bucket to merge markers into.

Returns:
    JSON response with the number of markers accepted/changed.

Raises:
    InvalidBucketNameError: If bucket name is invalid.
    BucketNotFoundError: If bucket does not exist.
    InvalidPathError: If the body is not a JSON object.

get.description:
Return the server's current timestamp for clock synchronization.

Clients use this endpoint to calculate clock offset via round-trip
measurement (NTP-like): the client records T1 before the request,
the server returns T2, and the client records T3 after the response.
Offset = T2 - (T1 + RTT/2), where RTT = T3 - T1.

Returns:
    JSON with ``{"timestamp": <float>}`` (Unix epoch seconds).

Health check endpoint.

Returns an empty response with 200 OK status to indicate
the server is healthy and accepting requests.

When ``size`` is supplied, returns that many bytes (bounded to
``HEALTH_MAX_PROBE_BYTES``) so a client can measure throughput for
auto-tuning. The payload is a deterministic NUL-byte string — never
reflected request input.

Returns:
    Empty string (200 OK response), or ``size`` NUL bytes.

Prometheus metrics endpoint.
